item.title: Rugelach
item.description: In Yiddish, Rugelach means little twists, which is the perfect way to describe these cookies. Flaky, butter dough is wrapped around an assortment of fillings like chocolate chips, fruit jams, and cinnamon sugar. The dough has cream cheese and sour cream incorporated, making it very easy to work with and roll out. We stuffed some with chocolate chips and others with a sweet and tangy jam. item.title: Easiest Ever Cinnamon Rolls
item.description: Um, yum!! Easy for sure... delicious definitely! These cinnamon rolls take a little effort and time, but they're by no means hard to make. The dough is soft and melts in your mouth. There's just enough butter and cinnamon for a wonderful gooey center. On top is a classic glaze that adds just the right amount of sweetness. If you have leftovers, they're fantastic heated in the microwave.

item.title: Crock Pot Christmas Crack
item.description: This super easy candy recipe is delicious. The chocolate is smooth and creamy - it kind of tastes like a cross between a Reese's cup and a Snickers bar. This recipe makes a huge batch of candy. It would be great on the dessert table or packaged in tins as a festive holiday gift.

item.title: Coconut Macaroons
item.description: Made with minimal ingredients, these coconut macaroons get slightly crispy and golden brown outside. The inside is sweet, sticky, and chewy. A delicious dessert if you're looking for a gluten-free or egg-free option. They'll satisfy all the coconut lovers in your life taste buds.

item.title: Pecan Fudge Pie
item.description: Love chocolate? Love pecans? You'll love this pecan fudge pie. It's rich and fudgy with crunchy pecans in every bite. The top forms a sugary crust once baked. Adding a dollop of whipped cream when serving is a delicious final touch. This simple-to-make pie will be a great addition to any holiday menu.

item.title: Stuffed Beef Tenderloin Recipe
item.description: Danny's stuffed beef tenderloin recipe is delicious. The beef is stuffed with sauteed mushrooms and scallions. The veggies help the meat maintain its moisture while the seasonings infuse the meat. It adds just the right touch of flavor without overpowering the beef tenderloin's natural flavor. Whether you serve on date night or as the centerpiece of a holiday meal, prepare for many oohs and ahhs. The meat is so tender it almost melts in your mouth with every bite.

item.title: Traditional Homestyle Mashed Potatoes
item.description: There are hundreds of ways to make mashed potatoes and even more opinions on how to do it. If you follow Kat's method you will have perfectly creamy mashed potatoes. We used a hand mixer to make sure there were no lumps. The trick to this recipe is to warm the butter, milk, and sour cream. Adding the warm ingredients to the hot potatoes keeps the potatoes hot but also helps the milk mixture distribute evenly. Sour cream is the secret ingredient. It adds a subtle flavor.

item.title: Holiday Cheddar Spread
item.description: The combination of cheese and alcohol makes this holiday cheddar spread feel like a fancy appetizer. We tried it with both wine and beer. It's super creamy and has a little tang from the aged cheddar cheese. There's a little bite from the onion, but it's not overpowering. This would be great to serve as an appetizer during the holidays or on New Year's Eve but also great at a tailgate or game night party. Yummy!

item.title: Hot Cocoa Cupcakes With Vanilla Bean Whipped Cream Icing
item.description: These hot cocoa cupcakes are fun and festive. We topped ours with mini marshmallows and crushed up candy canes for a festive feel. Toppings can be adjusted, though, to add whatever you enjoy on hot cocoa. The light and fluffy cupcakes are filled with chocolate flavor. On top is a whipped cream icing that's light in flavor and rich at the same time, thanks to vanilla beans. They're a fun winter dessert and a tasty spin on hot chocolate.

item.title: Holiday Spinach Casserole
item.description: This is one of those easy holiday casseroles that you can prepare ahead of time and just pop it in the oven when ready to eat. It is cheesy, creamy, and oh so good. The spinach flavor really shines through. So yummy!
